## Goal

A self-hostable remote server that serves many homes safely on a separate user-content domain, signs viewers in, lets an operating layer enforce its limits through ports, and gives cloud chat hosts a remote MCP server, so inline artifacts persist there.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| RM-03 | A self-hostable remote server hosts many homes behind one gateway with per-artifact origins on a separate user-content domain; the managed service's operating layer lives outside this repository and reaches the server only through operator ports | I, X | Container image serves two accounts' homes; cross-tenant reads, writes and frame entries are refused (seeded attempts); a grep and dependency audit shows no operator-layer code in the core |
| MC-04 | A remote MCP server over Streamable HTTP with OAuth (dynamic and metadata-document client registration, refresh tokens), stateless with explicit handles; inline MCP Apps in cloud chat hosts persist drafts, submissions and actions through it | I, X | Protocol suite against the remote endpoint; external: a claude.ai custom connector and a ChatGPT custom MCP server (formerly developer mode; write tools need a Business or Enterprise workspace, VERIFIED_FACTS) create, open and submit an artifact on a test deployment, opening it through its full-page link. Inline persistence of exported MCP Apps needs WP-17's exporter and app-only tools, which come later: WP-17 repeats this check inline through the remote MCP server (check boundary, D125) |
| HY-08 | Viewer identity on remote servers: optional OAuth sign-in, display names for anonymous viewers recorded as unverified; capability URLs remain the authorization | B | Signed-in and anonymous viewers record the right viewer kind; a forged identity claim is refused; a link without sign-in still works within its scopes |
| HY-09 | Hosted artifacts are served only from the user-content domain; the shell offers a report control in its own origin; a server policy can add an interstitial and an expiry to public links | B | Serving from the main domain is impossible (route test); the artifact can't click or hide the report control (forgery suite of WP-07 reused); interstitial and expiry honored |
| HO-09 | Operator ports on the remote server (limits, metering, account resolution, abuse actions) with no-op defaults for self-hosters | M, C | A fixture operator denies a share over its limit with a diagnostic, receives metering events, and suspends an artifact; with no operator everything works |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- the remote server mode: many homes, one gateway, per-artifact origins on the user-content domain, worker-mode frames;
- viewer sign-in and display names;
- the shell's report control, and policy hooks for interstitials and expiry;
- operator ports with no-op defaults;
- the remote MCP endpoint, so WP-17's MCP Apps persist in cloud chat hosts;
- a container image and self-hosting docs.

Design detail for this package:

- From WP-14 (D162): turn on the harness plugin's remote MCP server: `features.remoteMcp` in `tools/plugins/definition.ts` with `enabled: true`, the production `url` and the service's `privacyPolicyUrl` (Anthropic's directory asks a plugin with a remote server for one); the generator adds it to every manifest and the README, and the check holds both to `https:`. OpenAI's directory takes a local MCP server only from allowlisted partners, so this server, with OAuth and no plan display or upgrade prompt (D147; the plugin check refuses such words), is the plugin's MCP route there, and the route for surfaces that install no local plugin: ChatGPT and OpenAI's dots (account-installed plugins), Grok Bot (cloud skills and connectors) and Meta's Muse app (a reviewed connector). Record each surface's submission steps with Mirza (VERIFIED_FACTS, WP-14). In Anthropic's directory, WP-14's listing (submitted from `mostra-dev/mostra-plugin`, 2026-10-31) is listed on Claude Code only, because the Skill needs a local shell and a browser on the same machine: once the release carrying the remote server is published, tick **Cowork** and **Claude apps** on the plugin's **Settings** tab in the developer portal (claude.ai/directory/manage; no new submission), and submit the remote server as an **MCP connector** linked to the plugin (Anthropic's docs: a plugin that references a remote server you run submits it as a connector too), with OAuth, the privacy policy and a reviewer test account. Both need Mirza's sign-in; the portal's controls don't take an automated browser's clicks.
- WP-28 refines this specification (D123).
- Multi-home mode behind one gateway; per-artifact origins on the user-content domain, with worker-mode frames (D70).
- Operator ports with no-op defaults, so a self-hoster needs no operating layer; the managed service's operating layer reaches the server only through them (D116, HO-09).
- The remote MCP endpoint serves WP-15's transport-independent tool handlers over Streamable HTTP with OAuth (MC-04), so WP-17's MCP Apps persist in cloud chat hosts.
- Check boundary for MC-04 (D125 puts this package before WP-17): prove the endpoint, its authorization and an agent in a cloud chat host creating, opening (through the full-page link) and submitting an artifact. The MCP App exporter, its client transport and the app-only tools are WP-17's; WP-17 repeats the check inline through this server. Build nothing WP-17 would have to work around: the app-only tools of INTERFACES §12 are served by the same handlers.
- The report control renders in the shell's origin like every trusted control (invariant 7); policy hooks add an interstitial and an expiry to public links (HY-09).
- A container image and self-hosting docs; RM-03's audit shows no operating-layer code in the core.

## Out of scope

- The managed service's operating layer: accounts, billing, quotas, metering storage, abuse tooling and fleet operation (outside this repository, D116)
- `ee/` features (D118)
- Sandboxed remote execution (RM-06, v1.x)

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- ChatGPT's write tools on a custom MCP server need a Business or Enterprise workspace, and approved tool snapshots freeze (VERIFIED_FACTS, 2026-10-16): arrange the external check with Mirza early, and keep schemas additive (D32).
- Cross-tenant isolation is hygiene: seeded cross-tenant reads, writes and frame entries are negative tests, as WP-05's are.

## Handoff

Hosted links on a real remote server, and inline Mostra that persists in cloud chat hosts; WP-31 builds team features on its viewer identity.
